Blog Review: Nov. 25

2

Shares

PCIe SVC; co-packaged optics; liquid-cooled data center model; LUT-GEMM; automotive traceability.

November 25th, 2026 -

By: Jesse Allen

Cadence’s Igor Krause examines PCIe’s Streamlined Virtual Channel Extended Capability, which aims to address limitations of the traditional PCIe ordering model in modern multi-host fabrics by introducing a standardized approach for TC-to-VC assignment.
Synopsys’ Greg Sorber chats with Sanjay Gangadhara about co-packaged optics, including how it differs from pluggable modules, why the approach is gaining traction now, and what it will take to make it work at scale.
Siemens’ Benoit Honel simulates a 5.22 MW liquid-cooled AI data center pod together with its cooling plant, solar PV system, battery storage, and grid connection to determine how climate impacts cooling performance.
Arm’s Erick Amador explores when lookup-table GEMM can outperform traditional multiplication for ultra-low-bit LLMs, and how model shapes, packing, and hardware affect the result.
Keysight’s Katharine Edmonds highlights how connected design data and IP lifecycle management support long-term automotive semiconductor traceability.
Plus, check out blogs featured in the latest Manufacturing, Packaging & Materials and Systems & Design newsletters:
Amkor Technology’s Gerard John demonstrates why just meeting a spec is no longer sufficient.
Lam Research’s Taeyeon Oh illustrates how to model process variation, detect multiple failure modes, and evaluate DRAM solutions with less wafer experimentation.
Intel Foundry’s Lori Scott explains why trusted data is a critical starting point for intelligent chip manufacturing.
SEMI’s Sungho Yoon zeroes in on the explosion of new and upcoming production lines driving silicon wafer demand.
Axiomise’s Fabiana Muto explores how most re-spins are caused by logic and functional flaws, not hard-to-predict physical effects.
Keysight’s Chris Maloney explains why a component can meet its individual design targets and still behave differently as part of a complete optical link.
Cadence’s Paul Graykowski looks at the benefits of combining architectural proof, software-driven verification, simulation, emulation, and cloud-based compute infrastructure.
ChipAgents’ Emily Yan details how shortening the path from design intent to verified implementation could put custom silicon within reach of more teams.
Arteris’ Andy Nightingale demonstrates how to maintain consistent communication behavior, integration, and security across configurations.
Siemens EDA’s Ujjwal Negi and Prashant Dixit show how to validate UCIe.mem implementations across development stages while reusing a common verification environment.
